title: A Permanent Pokémon Store Is Finally Coming To London
summary:
The first of "several" outside Asia.

After years of us leaving the pop-up shop at the European International Championships and wondering, "why isn't this a permanent thing?", it seems our wishes have finally been answered.

The Pokémon Company has today announced that a "permanent, physical Pokémon store" is set to open in London. The store (not referred to as a 'Pokémon Center' in TPC's official statement, interestingly) will open by 2029, and will offer "a variety of exclusive merchandise and one-of-a-kind experiences for Trainers of all ages".

title: Strange Scaffold's Super Slick Revenge Shooter Is Out Now On Switch 2
summary:
Beast your eyes.

Strange Scaffold — the developer behind Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Tactical Takedown, El Paso, Elsewhere, Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator and more — announced last month that it was bringing its super slick FPS I Am Your Beast to Switch 1 and 2. Well, what do you know, it's available right now!

The game launched on the eShop yesterday (20th October), where it can now be found for $19.99. There's no sign of a listing on the EU storefront at the time of writing, but we're sure it won't be far behind.

Direct message.

title: Award-Winning Indie Horror 'Mouthwashing' Finally Arrives On Switch This Month
summary:
Eye spy.

Creepy space horror Mouthwashing became something of an indie sensation when it launched back in 2024. After racking up over 500,000 Steam sales, publisher Critical Reflex announced that a Switch version was in the works and now (a year on from that announcement), we finally have a release date.

As revealed in yesterday's Xbox Showcase, Mouthwashing will launch on the Switch eShop on 29th October — yep, as in next week. It's already available to pre-order on the North American storefront, in fact, for $12.99. We've noticed that the store lists its release date as 10th October, but we're sure that's just a typo (we've reached out to Critical Reflex just to double-check).

Ubisoft has shown strong support for the Switch 2 since its launch last year, bringing franchises such as Assassin's Creed to the system. Now, in a special 5th anniversary livestream this week, the Riders Republic team has announced a Switch 2 version of the game is on the way.

title: Pixel Art RPG 'Drova' Is Getting A Switch 2 Sequel Next Year
summary:
Torn to be Wild.

Developer Just2D and publisher Deck13 have announced that a sequel to the 2024 RPG Drova - Forsaken Kin is in the works, and it'll be coming to Switch 2 at some point next year.

Drova II - Torn Lands boasts the same pixel art aesthetic as its predecessor and continues its fantasy story, though it looks like the dev has aimed to go bigger and better this time around, with an expanded combat system, two central factions to choose between, and more story-influencing decisions to make.
